\section[o desacordo]{o desacordo — the disagreement}

\label{lesson:PT-C338-desacordo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to persuade, then the Portuguese for the firm belief.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o desacordo}
\textbf{o desacordo} — \textquotedblleft{}the disagreement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Estamos em desacordo sobre quase tudo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We disagree about almost everything.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Estar em desacordo} — to disagree.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{desacordo} is built from \emph{des-} and \emph{acordo} \textquotedblleft{}agreement\textquotedblright{}, from the verb \emph{acordar} in its old sense \textquotedblleft{}to agree\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Vulgar Latin \emph{accordāre}, a formation on Latin \emph{cor, cordis} \textquotedblleft{}heart\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o desacordo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o desacordo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o desacordo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to persuade, then the Portuguese for the firm belief, then say \emph{o desacordo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does o desacordo mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The disagreement\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[discordar]{discordar — to disagree}

\label{lesson:PT-C338-discordar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the firm belief, then the Portuguese for the disagreement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: discordar}
\textbf{discordar} — \textquotedblleft{}to disagree\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Discordo de ti: o filme não é nada aborrecido.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I disagree with you: the film is not boring at all.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Discordar de alguém} — to disagree with someone. Politely: \emph{permite-me discordar}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{discordar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{discordāre} \textquotedblleft{}to be at variance, to differ\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{discors}, built from \emph{dis-} \textquotedblleft{}apart\textquotedblright{} and \emph{cor, cordis} \textquotedblleft{}heart\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{discordar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{discordar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{discordar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the firm belief, then the Portuguese for the disagreement, then say \emph{discordar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does discordar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To disagree\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[objetar]{objetar — to object}

\label{lesson:PT-C338-objetar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the disagreement, then the Portuguese for to disagree.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: objetar}
\textbf{objetar} — \textquotedblleft{}to object\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ninguém objetou quando ela propôs uma pausa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Nobody objected when she suggested a break.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Objetar que…} — to object that… Formal; AO90 spelling, older \emph{objectar}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{objetar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{obiectāre} \textquotedblleft{}to throw before or against, to set against\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), formed on \emph{obicere}, built from \emph{ob} \textquotedblleft{}against\textquotedblright{} and \emph{iacere} \textquotedblleft{}to throw\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{objetar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{objetar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{objetar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the disagreement, then the Portuguese for to disagree, then say \emph{objetar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[a objeção]{a objeção — the objection}

\label{lesson:PT-C338-objecao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to disagree, then the Portuguese for to object.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a objeção}
\textbf{a objeção} — \textquotedblleft{}the objection\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Alguma objeção? Então começamos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Any objections? Then we begin.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Fazer uma objeção} — to raise an objection. Older spelling \emph{objecção}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{objeção} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{obiectiō} \textquotedblleft{}a throwing or putting before\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), from \emph{obicere} \textquotedblleft{}to throw against\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{iacere} \textquotedblleft{}to throw\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[contradizer]{contradizer — to contradict}

\label{lesson:PT-C338-contradizer}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to object, then the Portuguese for the objection.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: contradizer}
\textbf{contradizer} — \textquotedblleft{}to contradict\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O meu irmão contradiz tudo o que eu digo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My brother contradicts everything I say.}
\end{quote}

Conjugated like \emph{dizer}: \emph{contradigo, contradizes, contradiz}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{contradizer} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{contrādīcere} \textquotedblleft{}to speak against\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built from \emph{contrā} \textquotedblleft{}against\textquotedblright{} and \emph{dīcere} \textquotedblleft{}to say\textquotedblright{}; Portuguese reshaped it on \emph{dizer}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
